observations: Photo shows a game console fully covered in a camouflage-pattern skin/wrap, so its actual shell shape, logos, and ports are not visible.
No Sony logo, model number, or serial sticker is visible anywhere on the unit.
A power cable with a UK-style plug and an HDMI cable are shown coiled on the box.
Two sealed red boxes labeled 'Wireless Controller' and 'X6' sit on top; one box partly reads 'FOR [PS?]' but no Sony/DualShock branding is visible.
No photo shows the console powered on, a home screen, or any back-panel port layout.
Background shows a glass display cabinet with other electronics, consistent with a resale shop, not proof of this specific unit's condition.

identity.kind: game console, seller claims PS4 Slim

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows the unit fully wrapped in a camo skin, hiding the shell shape and any Sony/model markings needed to confirm it is a Slim rather than an original or Pro.
No power-on, boot screen, or gameplay clip is shown in photo 0.

Photo 0 shows two sealed boxes marked 'Wireless Controller' and 'X6', but no Sony or DualShock branding is visible, so they appear to be third-party accessories rather than confirmed official controllers.

risks.risk: Console model cannot be confirmed (Slim vs original vs Pro) because the camo skin hides the shell shape and any model text.
risks.proof: A photo of the console with the skin removed, or at least the back panel and side profile, plus a close-up of the model/serial label.

risks.risk: Unit may not power on or may have internal faults (overheating, HDD failure, disc drive issues if applicable).
risks.proof: A video of the console powering on to the home screen and reading a disc or digital game.

risks.risk: Bundled controllers may be unofficial/third-party rather than genuine Sony DualShock, affecting bundle value.
risks.proof: A photo of the controller itself (unboxed) showing branding/logo.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic/third-party controllers, not genuine

risks.risk: Storage capacity (HDD size) is unknown and affects value.
risks.proof: A photo of the system settings storage screen or the rear label stating GB capacity.
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lowest common capacity (500GB)

risks.risk: Camo wrap could be concealing cosmetic damage, cracks, or a mismatched/refurbished shell.
risks.proof: A photo with the skin peeled back or removed at one corner to show the shell underneath.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming possible hidden cosmetic damage

proof_requests: Photo of the console with the camo skin removed or peeled back, showing the bare shell, Sony logo, and model/serial sticker.
Video of the console powered on to the PS4 home screen.
Photo of the system storage settings screen showing HDD capacity.
Unboxed photo of one of the 'Wireless Controller' units showing its branding/logo clearly.
response.reason: The camo skin obscures every identifying feature (shape, logo, model/serial), so even a worst-case price cannot be set without knowing whether this is truly a PS4 Slim or a different variant, and no power-on proof is shown.
